data.gender_notes: Haricharan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Haricharan is derived from two Sanskrit words: Hari (God) and Charan (footstep or chariot). The name signifies that the deity's presence or blessings are always with the person and that they are on the divine path. The name Haricharan carries the meaning “God's chariot” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Haricharan usually hope their child will grow to embody god's chariot and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Haricharan was a famous poet and musician during the medieval period in India, who was known for his devotion to Lord Vishnu. He lived during the 14th and 15th centuries and is believed to have composed many poems and songs in praise of Vishnu.

Haricharan is also known as Haridasa, a prominent member of the Haridasa movement. Haridasas were wandering minstrels who dedicated their lives to spreading the message of love and devotion to Vishnu through music and poetry. They lived during the 15th and 16th centuries and were influential in Hindu religious and cultural life in South India.
